meta.channel_definition: GA4 default channel grouping. 'Organic Search' = unpaid search engine traffic (google/bing organic). 'Organic Shopping' (free Google Shopping listings) and 'Organic Video' are exposed separately as daily series so you can build an 'all non-paid organic' view if desired. Paid Search is NOT included.
meta.metric_notes: sessions/engaged_sessions/purchases/revenue are GA4-additive and safe to sum across days. engagement_rate is recomputed as engaged/sessions per period, never summed. purchases = ecommerce_purchases; revenue = purchase_revenue (GA4 attribution, differs from Shopify True Gross).
meta.bot_filtering: sessions and engaged_sessions are CLEAN BY DEFAULT: on days inside a listed contaminated_periods window, the bot burst is removed via baseline substitution (median of surrounding clean days). Consumers should just read `sessions` and get clean numbers -- no client-side correction needed. The original GA4 values are preserved as `sessions_raw`/`engaged_sessions_raw`, and any affected daily/period row carries `contaminated: true` + `bot_excluded_sessions`. purchases/revenue are left raw (bots convert ~0). See contaminated_periods for the windows and the source registry (ga4_bot_windows table).

contaminated_periods.reason: Automated google/organic-mislabeled desktop bot burst (Windows-Chrome / proxy-datacenter geo, sub-15s engagement, near-zero conversion). ~3.3k contaminated sessions.
contaminated_periods.detection_method: detect_ga4_bot_windows.py: multi-day session spike (>=1.8x local baseline) + desktop skew (>=68%) + collapsed engagement (<=45% of baseline sec/sess) + near-zero conversion; confirmed in GA4 UI (browser/OS + geo not in DB).
